title: Flex Direction
definition: Utilities for controlling the direction in which flex items are placed in the flex container.
simpleExplanation: Flexbox normally puts things in a horizontal Row. If you change it to `flex-col`, it stacks things vertically in a Column. The brilliant part is that you can use responsive classes to have a Row on Desktop, but a Column on Mobile.
realWorldExample: A Pricing Page with 3 pricing tiers. On a laptop, you want them side-by-side (`flex-row`). On a mobile phone, there isn't enough room, so you stack them vertically (`flex-col`).

basic: What is the default direction of a `flex` container?
intermediate: How do you completely reverse the visual order of items in a flex container without changing the HTML?

answers.question: Reverse visual order?
answers.answer: Use `flex-row-reverse` or `flex-col-reverse`. The item written first in the HTML will magically appear last on the screen.
